methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI bills faced a logjam in the General Assembly due to a Trump executive order, but Congress is working to fill the gap
signals.signal_reading: Federal policy uncertainty freezing state AI legislation while threatening broadband funding creates a double barrier to distributed AI capability, particularly in regions like Southwest Virginia that depend on federal infrastructure investment to enable any meaningful AI adoption.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Young workforce facing AI displacement pressure in Richmond signals shallow adoption anxiety without corresponding depth-building infrastructure, suggesting concentration of AI capability concerns in metro areas while rural regions remain disconnected from the conversation entirely.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA represents intentional community-facing AI education infrastructure that could enable peer-to-peer capability building beyond elite tech circles, testing whether metro institutions can seed distributed fluency rather than hoarding expertise.

signals.title: Danville to consider data center tax increase, development guidelines
signals.signal_reading: Danville pursuing data center infrastructure positions the historically underserved region as AI infrastructure host rather than AI capability developer—extracting tax revenue from shallow platform deployment without building local technical depth or workforce AI fluency.

signals.title: Teaching AI by Doing, Not Studying - Inside Higher Ed
signals.signal_reading: Pedagogy shift toward learning-by-doing rather than studying AI theory signals potential pathway to distributed deep capability if implemented across Virginia's educational institutions, though success depends on whether resources reach beyond elite universities into community colleges and rural schools.
